subject: Problem initializing state at first capture: logProb is NA or NaN

messages.author: 7cb2eb89472f7169
messages.subject: Problem initializing state at first capture: logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to run a multi-event capture-recapture model, but runMCMC is returning the following warning messages for the initial state (z) at first capture of each individual:

 

warning: problem initializing stochastic node z[1, 9]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: problem initializing stochastic node z[2, 18]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: problem initializing stochastic node z[3, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.

Etc.

 

I am familiar with the error logProb is -Inf, but I don’t really understand the meaning of logProb is NA or NaN in this context. Indeed, for each individual, I provide an initial value of state at first capture (and at all subsequent) that:

-        is compatible with the observation y (if it wasn’t the case I suspect I would get “logProb y[1, 9] is  -Inf” anyway)

-        is compatible with the following observations and underlying state (i.e. no impossible state transitions are specified in the initial values; similarly, if it wasn’t the case I suspect I would get “logProb z[2, 9] is  -Inf”)

 

So I am a bit lost as to what can cause such a warning message. I would be very grateful is anyone can spot what’s wrong in my code.

 

The transition and observation matrices are quite large, so I attached an R script with my code, as well as a subset of the data that can be used to reproduce the error. The size of the matrices (that are time- and individual-depednent) is also the reason why “calculate = F” in nimbleModel.

 

Thank you,

Marwan

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Problem initializing state at first capture: logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
Hi Marwan,

As a first step, please take a look at these suggestions for diagnosing initialization issues. A logProb of NA like this usually means that when the *prior* for, say, `z[1,9]` is being computed that there is an NA in one of the parameters of the prior, so it may simply be that you need to initialize other nodes in the model.

-chris

messages.author: 7cb2eb89472f7169
messages.subject: Re: Problem initializing state at first capture: logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
Hi Chris,

Thank you for your suggestion, it helped me find the error. In case it can help somebody else, here it is:


The state (z) at first capture (f) is drawn from a categorical distribution:   z[i, f[i]] ~ dcat( S0[1:16] )

with S0 being the proportion of each state at first capture computed from the data.

For some reason, S0 contained only NA when I looked at it (using the command nimble_model$S0, nimble_model being the output of the nimbleModel function). This resulted in logProb is NA or NaN.for z at first capture. S0 was specified within the model using the following lines:

S0[1] <- prop[1]             

S0[2] <- prop[2]

...

S0[15] <- prop[15]

S0[16] <- 1-sum(prop[1:15])

With prop being a vector containing the proportion of each state at first capture computed from the data and provided as a constant to the model.

I then realized that instead of providing prop as a constant, and then calculating S0 from prop within the model, I could directly provide S0 as a constant. This solved the problem, since S0 was no longer NA. It remains unclear to me why the attributions S0[1] <- prop[1], S0[2] <- prop[2], etc. did not work resulting in S0 being NA.


Marwan

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Problem initializing state at first capture: logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
hi Marwan,

I'm glad you figured out a work-around.

I think the reason that `S0` is not being set based on `prop` is that you are using `calculate=FALSE` in your call to `nimbleModel`. There are good reasons for doing that if you don't want the whole model calculated in uncompiled code, which can be slow for big models. But it also means that `S0` is not being set.  I think when the MCMC is initialized that `S0` should be populated then and that the warnings you initially reported might be something that could be ignored, but I haven't looked carefully. One could also directly call `calculate('S0')` to specifically get the `S0` populated.

In any event, that is all just to try to clarify some things given you got things working.

-chris
